correctness.rationale: Connected cographs of order at least 9 are forced to have a universal vertex under \(K_{2,5}\)-avoidance. Removing it is exactly equivalent to imposing \(\Delta(H)\le4\) and \(K_{2,4}\)-avoidance on the remainder. The fully inspected \(K_{2,4}\) theorem bounds remainder components by six vertices and gives the sharp six-vertex weight 11. The resulting finite component optimization has deficits \((2,3,3,2,0,1)\), whose exact modulo-five minima are \((0,1,2,3,2)\). Boundary orders 7 and 8 and disconnected graphs are separately bounded. A standalone verifier exhausts the local six-vertex graph problem and replays the integer optimization and constructions.

It determines every order, a sharp structural threshold at \(n=9\), and all large extremizers.
